## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

## Quality Check

code chunk that checks all forward read & reverse read files

```{r}
# loading required library
library(dada2)

# forward read quality
plotQualityProfile((fnFs))

# reverse read quality
plotQualityProfile((fnRs))
```

## Filtering and Trimming

code chunk that estimates and visualizes error rates

```{r}
# loading required library
library(dada2)

# sequence error rate
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=T)

# visualize learned errors for filtered reverse reads
plotErrors(errR, nominalQ=TRUE)
```

export reverse read error plot as pdf

```{r}
p <- plotErrors(errR, nominalQ=TRUE)
ggsave(filename = here::here("outputs", "ReverseReadErrorPlot.pdf"),
       plot = p, 
       width = 10,
       height = 10,
       units = "in")
```

Error plots are not similar for forward and reverse reads

## Data Polishing Part2

ASVs with no species and genus: ASV22 (phylum firmicutes) & ASV207 (phylum Actinobacteria)

### Top hits for ASV22:

g-proteobacteria has a top hit with E-value of 2e-33 & percent identity of 86.49%.

### Top hits for ASV207:

firmicutes has a top hit with E-value of 4e-20 & oercent identity of 63.86%.

No, we can not resolve species as percent identity is too low. Also, running against clusteredNR gives the name of clusteres ncestor not the exact species name.

## Alpha diversity visualization

Exporting table as a csv file

```{r}
write.csv(rnd, "outputs/rnd.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Plot diversity and richness estimations

```{r}
# loading required library
library("ggplot2")
library("RColorBrewer")
ggplot(rndl, aes (x=dpw, y=Value, color = Estimator, fill= Estimator))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge())+
  facet_grid(rd~category, scales = "free") + 
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + theme_bw()
```

## save plot as pdf

```{r}
ggsave(filename = here::here("outputs", "diversityRichnessPlot.pdf"),
       plot = p, 
       width = 10,
       height = 8,
       units = "in")
```
